A soft approach to understand the world

The Lin Lab aims to understand human physiology through novel bioelectronics and continuous ultrasound imaging. We combine materials, device engineering, integrated electronics, and computational methods to observe physiological processes over time, with the long-term goal of enabling more accessible and personalized healthcare.

RESEARCH INTERESTS

Continuous Ultrasound Imaging

We develop wearable ultrasound systems that continuously visualize deep tissues and monitor organ function. Our research combines skin-conformal transducers and imaging methods to capture dynamic physiological changes.

Novel Bioelectronics

We develop soft bioelectronic devices for continuous physiological monitoring. By combining advanced materials, sensor design, miniaturized electronics, and wireless integration, we aim to create practical tools for measuring the human body during everyday activities.

Understanding Human Physiology

We investigate how cardiovascular function, metabolism, and organ activity interact in health and disease. By combining novel imaging, biomarker measurements, and machine learning, we aim to uncover physiological insights and advance personalized health monitoring.

Muyang Lin, Ph.D.

Principal InvestigatorIncoming Assistant Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering, HKUST

Muyang Lin is an incoming Assistant Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering at HKUST, joining in July 2027. He obtained his B.S. in Measurement and Control Technology and Instruments from Tianjin University, followed by his Ph.D. in Nanoengineering from the University of California, San Diego. Working with Prof. Sheng Xu, he developed wearable ultrasound systems for continuous monitoring of deep tissues and cardiovascular function. He subsequently pursued postdoctoral research at UC San Diego and Stanford University, advancing soft biomedical devices and wearable sensing technologies.

His research combines novel bioelectronics, continuous ultrasound imaging, and multimodal sensing to understand human physiology and enable personalized health monitoring. By integrating device engineering, biomarker measurements, and machine learning, he aims to reveal how cardiovascular function, metabolism, and organ activity interact in health and disease. His interdisciplinary background spans materials science, electronic systems, biomedical imaging, and translational research.
